caveats: multiple comparisons: two candidate configurations were tested against the same baseline, which gives two chances to pass the rule by luck; the rule does not correct for it
the perturbation set is machine-stripped text: no typos and no abbreviations beyond the original questions; it is a robustness test, not a substitute for real queries
dev sets are small (19 answerable product items, 14 policy items); most intervals are wide and query-style cells with fewer than 8 items are marked too_small_to_interpret

exact score ties inside a branch (frequent in the folded branch: equal-length documents with the same matching tokens) are broken by stable key, client-side (DECISIONS R25): an arbitrary but fixed rule, so part of any measured difference may come from that arbitrary order

dense_sparse_folded has two lexical branches of three, so dense carries 1/3 of the RRF weight instead of 1/2 as in the baseline and in dense_folded: its effect mixes 'a new signal' with 'less dense weight'
